headline: Actor Don arrested at Dhaka airport as Salman Shah murder accused arrested
summary: Mohammad Ashraful Haque, known as Don, was detained by immigration police while attempting to travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah.
details: Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka today.
Ashraful was detained at the airport and subsequently handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for further investigation.
The arrest follows a court directive and a requisition from the investigation officer to prevent the accused named in the FIR of the murder case filed with Ramna Police Station.
Ashraful had arrived at the airport around 6:00 am today to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
The case involves the death of actor Salman Shah, who was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence in Dhaka on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.

Ashraful had arrived at the airport around 6:00 am today to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.

The case involves the death of actor Salman Shah, who was found dead at his Eskaton Road residence in Dhaka on September 6, 1996, at the age of 25.

headline_marked: India says [[Tarique-Modi talks could resolve issues]] between Dhaka and New Delhi
headline: India says Tarique-Modi talks could resolve issues between Dhaka and New Delhi
summary: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi expresses confidence that a meeting between the two leaders would sort out problems amid renewed discussions of a visit to India.
details: Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi stated that many issues between Dhaka and New Delhi could be resolved if Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet.

Speaking after inaugurating a children's playing area at the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC), Trivedi described both leaders as 'people's persons' and expressed full confidence in a positive outcome.
The remarks come as discussions resume regarding a possible visit by PM Tarique Rahman to India, including a bilateral invitation extended in February 2026.
India has also invited PM Tarique Rahman to attend the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13 in his capacity as the chair of BIMSTEC.

The prospect of closer engagement follows fresh tensions between the two nations after a recent virtual speech by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi, which sparked outrage in Bangladesh.
The Indian government has reiterated that it had 'no role' in the event organized by a private media entity and did not endorse the remarks made by Sheikh Hasina.
Meanwhile, the Indian envoy also noted that the capacity for Indian visa processing is gradually increasing to meet growing demand.
caption:
Can a direct meeting between PM Tarique Rahman and PM Narendra Modi fix the current diplomatic tensions?

Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi stated that many issues between Dhaka and New Delhi could be resolved if Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi meet.

Speaking after inaugurating a children's playing area at the Indian Visa Application Centre (IVAC), Trivedi described both leaders as 'people's persons' and expressed full confidence in a positive outcome.

The remarks come as discussions resume regarding a possible visit by PM Tarique Rahman to India, including a bilateral invitation extended in February 2026.

India has also invited PM Tarique Rahman to attend the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12-13 in his capacity as the chair of BIMSTEC.

The prospect of closer engagement follows fresh tensions between the two nations after a recent virtual speech by ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi, which sparked outrage in Bangladesh.

The Indian government has reiterated that it had 'no role' in the event organized by a private media entity and did not endorse the remarks made by Sheikh Hasina.

Meanwhile, the Indian envoy also noted that the capacity for Indian visa processing is gradually increasing to meet growing demand.
